LESSON: CHEMICAL FAMILIES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.2: Chemical Families
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Chemical Families, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are elements suited for their use in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify chemical families in the periodic table,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Families in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. classify elements of the periodic table into their chemical families,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Families in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. investigate the physical and chemical properties of selected

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Chemical Families in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search for information on the categories of elements in the periodic table (alkali, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases and transition metals) and present in the plenary. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Chemical Families together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: as the learner carries out activities to investigate the reaction of sodium, magnesium and chlorine with air

and dilute acids.

● Digital literacy: as the learner uses available digital and print media to research on transition elements and their uses.

Values:
Love: as the learner takes care of self and others by observing safety when carrying out activities to investigate properties

of elements of the periodic table and appropriately using first aid kits in case of injuries.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Road safety: as the learner discusses with peers the properties of elements that make them suitable for use in illuminating

roads.
